name: Financial Aid in Plain Language
title: Financial Aid in Plain Language
answer: Financial aid in plain language means using AI to draft clear, simple guides to the FAFSA and to explain common problems families face, while keeping official details sourced from Federal Student Aid and having a person help with the form itself. It matters because the form confuses many families, and students who do not complete it miss aid they qualify for. Personalized, school-connected help works where general national campaigns do not.

sections.body: The federal financial aid form, the FAFSA, is a major hurdle for many families. It asks for tax information and involves steps that confuse even well educated parents. Students who do not complete it often miss out on aid they qualify for. Plain language help can make a difference. The idea is to use AI to draft plain language guides to the FAFSA and to explain common problems, so that families can understand the steps and complete the form.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: Counselors can use AI to draft plain language guides to the FAFSA and to explain common problems. Financial aid nights are a good place to combine these supports. A school can offer guides in families' languages, explain the steps, and have staff available to help families fill out the form. The text does not give grade bands for this idea. It does note that Chapter 14 described how to translate materials with human review, and that financial aid information is too important to leave to an unchecked translation.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels this evidence as a multidistrict trial. That trial found that personalized text messages based on each student's FAFSA status improved completion and college enrollment (Page et al., 2020). The messages told students exactly where they stood and what to do next. National campaigns without that personal connection did not work (Bird et al., 2021). The book states that the connection to real data and a real school made the difference.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Official information from Federal Student Aid at studentaid.gov should be the source for all details, since rules change. Families should never enter tax or identity information into a general chat tool. A counselor or trained volunteer should help families with the form itself. Translation of financial aid materials should have human review, because financial aid information is too important to leave to an unchecked translation. The decisions about the form and the family's information stay with a person, not with the AI tool.
